newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria starts currency board talks next week.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria starts currency board talks next week.

text.p: Bulgaria will resume talks next week with the IMF, on the implementation of a fixed exchange rate regime which is expected to stabilise the crumbling financial system, interim prime Minister Stefan Sofianski said on Friday.
"Bulgaria needs a currency board and negotiations on its implementation will begin next with a mission of the International Monetary Fund," Sofianski told a news conference.
The Fund proposed the implementation of a currency board last year to halt the freefall of the national currency, the lev, and to restore confidence in ailing banks.
The system requires levs in circulation to be matched by central bank reserves, severely curbing financial powers of the government and the central bank.
Opposition demands for early elections and the refusal of the ruling ex-communists to yield produced a political deadlock which was resolved after 30 days of mass protests.
President Petar Stoyanov, elected on the opposition ticket in November, brokered an agreement to hold early polls on April 19. On Wednesday he appointed an interim cabinet headed by Sofianski.
